title: S3 bucket with list-objects and get-object for anonymous users
user: Subdomain enumeration found assets.example.com which CNAMEs to assets.example.com.s3.amazonaws.com. The bucket name is 'example-assets-prod'. Testing: aws s3 ls s3://example-assets-prod --no-sign-request lists all objects. The bucket contains: backups/db_dump_2024.sql.gz (1.2 GB), config/production.yml, static/js/main.abc123.js.
assistant:
RECON: S3 bucket 'example-assets-prod' allows anonymous ListObjects and GetObject. The bucket policy grants s3:ListBucket and s3:GetObject to Principal: "*". Contents include database dumps and configuration files — this is a production data leak.

HYPOTHESIS: S3 bucket misconfiguration (CWE-284). The bucket is intended for static assets but contains sensitive data. Two attack vectors: (1) direct data exfiltration — download the database dump and config file, (2) supply chain — the JS bundle in static/js/ may contain API keys or internal endpoints.

TEST: minimum probe:
1. Confirm anonymous read access: aws s3 cp s3://example-assets-prod/config/production.yml /tmp/ --no-sign-request
2. Check config/production.yml for database credentials, API keys, JWT secrets, SMTP creds
3. Download a small sample of db_dump_2024.sql.gz to confirm it's not encrypted
4. Inspect main.abc123.js (source map?) for internal API endpoints and hardcoded keys
5. Check bucket versioning: aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket example-assets-prod --no-sign-request (may reveal deleted secrets in older versions)

INDICATOR: the config file contains valid database credentials, or the JS bundle contains API keys that authenticate to internal services.

Chainability: S3 bucket → config file → database credentials → direct database access → data exfiltration. OR: S3 bucket → JS bundle → internal API endpoint → SSRF from API → internal services.
